# Review — ani-017-e

## Pass 1

Checks run by script: the glyph sequence of units.json equals the packet's exactly (125 packet words, 443 signs, same codes in the same order); rubric flags match the packet word by word (41 rubric words in the units = the packet's 40, with Budge's rubric group erṭāit-nef split into rdyt + n·f); the one restored sign (D37 in rdyt) is flagged and no other; every word's morph covers all its glyphs; every `q` has one index per glyph and the splits/joins (in + n·f, rdyt + n·f, m-sꜣ, pḥ·n) are re-indexed correctly. Names and `say` agree with the published parts (Khepri, Ra, Isis, Nephthys, Anubis, Osiris, Shu, Atum, Horus, Seth, Ruti, Neni-nesu, Ani); pw tr rf sw, ky ḏd, wꜥbt, swꜣ, m-sꜣ, iṯ (V13 + D54), rwti, ṯs-pẖr follow the published spellings and renderings.

### Changes
- U0 · l · minor · "were-brought" for a singular subject (msyt) and against i "was brought" · changed to "was-brought".
- U0 · n · minor · msyt "evening meal" and ṯḥnt "faience" were presented as "taken as" without saying the sense is doubtful · added a sentence: both are the best the signs give but not sure; a meal "of faience" is strange, Budge takes ṯḥnt for a plant; the bead-collar sign (if rightly read) and the mineral grains are why faience is preferred.
- U4 · l, i · minor · ḥsw "filth" given as certain in l/i though Aa2 is approximate (one reader F52) and the reading of the word is a guess · "filth(?)" in l and i.
- U4 · n · minor · same: added "the reading is not sure" after the ḥs identification.
- U4 · n · minor · grg said to be written "as in the Spell 125 address"; the address writes grg g-r with T14, no U17; the U17 spelling with g and r as complements is the published weighing of the heart · reference changed to "the weighing of the heart".
- U10 · n · minor · the stray Q1 (Budge's "(sic)") was left unread, i.e. treated as a doubled sign, but the note did not use the misprint formula and mixed this with alternatives it says do not fit · note now opens "The papyrus writes the seat twice, st wsir; read wsir."; the alternatives (st "seat", ꜣst) are kept as considered and set aside. Glyphs unchanged (Q1 stays, role phon, empty tr, as published unread signs such as Z9 in rf).
- U11 · morph · minor · lemma "snt" for "found, lay out (a building)": the lemma is snṯ; the signs write t · lemma changed to snṯ, reading left snt (what the signs write).
- U11 · n · minor · same: note now says snṯ written with t for ṯ (as with iṯ·n·f, l. 131).
- U11 · n · minor · agentless passive "built (by) Atum" not clearly marked doubtful · added "so the reading is not sure" after the supplied in "by".
- U11 · i · style · "the Double Lion" against the published rendering "Double-Lion" (Spell 125 declarations) · changed to "the Double-Lion".
- U12 · l, i, n · major · twri ḥr nṯrty stẖ read as two active transitive verbs, "Horus purifies, Seth makes divine", with no object written, and nṯrty glossed "make divine" from nṯri, which is "be divine" (the causative would be s-nṯr); the note also called nṯrty "in the same form as twri" though it has an ending ty that twri lacks · re-read as two sentences of quality, verb before noun: "pure is Horus, divine(?) is Seth", twr "be clean, pure" (as the address takes twri, a state) and nṯri "be divine"; endings i / ty said to be unexplained; the active reading is mentioned and why it is weaker; the closing sentence now ties the sense to ṯs-pẖr. l: "has-arrived · the-remedy(?) · pure · Horus · divine(?) · Seth · and-vice-versa"; i: "The remedy(?) has arrived: Horus is pure and Seth is divine(?), and the other way round."

### Refused / checked and left
- U0 in n·f as passive sḏm "was brought": the alternative in·n·f (sḏm·n·f) is stated; the passive is supported by the gloss's rdyt n·f. Left.
- U0 tꜣnnt: X1 before U30 as `comp` t, M22 M22 as n n with N35 N35 complements — matches published nn (M22 M22 N35 N35). Left.
- U1 tr with M17 `phon i` not in the reading: same as published ani-017-a/c. Left.
- U3 bntt "baboons(?)" — marked "(?)" and "The reading is uncertain"; Budge agrees on the sense (apes); the feminine-dual idea is offered as a possibility only. Left.
- U3 ꜣst Q1 `log ꜣs`: matches published. Left.
- U5 ꜥfdt with t written before d: graphic grouping (X1 over D46), not a slip; the note says so. No misprint formula. Left.
- U5 mꜥẖtw "innards(?)": marked doubtful in l, i and n; F32 and F51 approximate. Left.
- U5 ẖr (T28) as "holding": new lemma ẖr kept distinct from ḫr "before" (the weighing of the heart files T28 under ḫr; that is the published part's matter, not this draft's).
- U6 rdyt "was given": a vague label, but the note says the ending yt is unexplained and gives the participle alternative; the quoted-clause reading after ir fits the answer wsir pw. Left.
- U8 qnqn "beating(?)" with nt that does not agree: marked doubtful, alternative ("the Beater of the Two Lands") given, the difficulty of nt stated. Left.
- U8 nni-nsw with X1 `phon t` not read: matches published (ani-017-a: "the t is part of the writing of nsw and not read"). Left.
- U10 smꜣt "place of union(?)": marked doubtful, burial sense mentioned as possible. New lemma smꜣt (the known smꜣ is "kill"). Left.
- U11 rwti: E23 phon / E23 comp as in ani-spell125-opening; V13 for t explained. Left.
- U12 rrt "remedy(?)": marked doubtful; Budge "drugs" agrees on sense. Left.
- U13 iṯ·n·f with V13 `phon iṯ` + D54 `det` and X1 as complement: as published ani-017-b (iṯt). Left.
- U14 ntf tm "He is Atum": plain nominal sentence; the wording is forced by the grammar, not taken from Budge. Left.
- No Budge-isms in any l / i ("triumphant" in Budge's mꜣꜥ-ḫrw rendered "true of voice"; no "saith", "homage").

## Pass 2

Checks run by script (scratch `check.py`): the glyph codes of units.json equal the packet's in order (443 signs); rubric flags agree sign by sign; the one restored sign is D37 in rdyt; every `q` indexes its glyphs 0…n−1 and equals the packet's `q` wherever the word is Budge's group unchanged (the six splits/joins — in + n·f, rdyt + n·f, m-sꜣ, pḥ·n — re-indexed correctly; Budge's "—" carried as no `q`); every morph covers all its glyphs; no `det` carries a `tr`; the per-glyph `tr` of each word against its `reading` (differences are only the y written with two reeds, unwritten endings — msyt, imt, tꜣwy, iryw, nṯrw, rdwy·f — the graphic order of wsir, ꜥfdt and nni-nsw, and signs the notes say are not read); no "triumphant / saith / homage / thy / hath" in any l or i. New lemmas recomputed from the morph lemmas absent from known-lemmas.json: the same 14 as gloss.json and new-lemmas.txt; the `__broaden__` entry for m starts with the known entry whole.

### Changes
- U11 / U12 · glyphs (O34 in snt, stẖ) · minor · the bolt O34 had `tr` "s"; the conventions write z where the sign is the bolt, and every published part does (stẖ, sipw, st, ḏs·f: O34/z) · `tr` set to "z" (readings stay snt, stẖ).
- U10 · n · minor · the note opened with the misprint formula but then hedged it ("Most likely … It could also be taken as …"), which is the opposite of what the formula claims · formula kept (see below) and the note rewritten to give the reason: the scribe began wsir with its seat and then wrote the whole group; this papyrus never writes st or ꜣst with a bare seat (st with t and the house, ꜣst with t and the egg, as in line 124), and "the place of union of the seat of Osiris" is an empty phrase. Glyphs unchanged.
- about · minor · "filth and lying", "the innards of Osiris" stated as sure where l / i / n mark both doubtful · "filth(?)", "innards(?)".
- U12 · n · style · the note quoted "divine is Seth" without the "(?)" that l and i carry · "divine(?) is Seth".
- U11 · n · style · pass 1 changed i to "Double-Lion" but the note still had "the Double Lion" twice · both changed to "Double-Lion" (the published form).
- gloss msyt · style/minor · "the meal laid on the table" and "written with the three skins ms and a table" describe this line's spelling (the table R3 is itself an approximate coding), not the lemma; the notes call the reading not sure but the entry had no "(?)" · now "msyt — evening meal (?) (noun f.; Budge: mesi)".
- gloss bntt · minor · "perhaps a feminine dual, 'the two female baboons'" is the note's suggestion for this line, not a fact of the lemma · removed.
- gloss ẖr · minor · line-specific quote "ntt ẖr 'which holds'" · removed. The sense "carrying, holding" is kept: it is a standard use of the preposition (what is "under" someone is what he carries or holds), so it is not invented.
- gloss qd · minor · line-specific quote "qd pr·k 'your house is built'" (which also presupposes the doubtful passive) · now "to build (verb; written with the man building a wall; Budge: qeṭ)" — A35 is the general sign of the word.
- gloss snṯ · style · "written snt" read as a fact of this line · "also written snt, with t for ṯ" (a general later spelling).
- gloss nṯri · minor · line-specific quote "nṯri stẖ 'divine is Seth'" · removed; "(?)" kept, as the note only "takes" the word for nṯri.
- gloss __broaden__ m · minor · the new sense quoted this line ("msyt m ṯḥnt 'a meal of faience'") · now "also \"of, made of\" (naming the material a thing is made of)". m of material is sound (a regular use of m) and is kept.

### Refused / checked and left
- U10 misprint formula — asked to re-examine whether the formula is justified, since the drafter had listed st "seat" and ꜣst "Isis" as other possibilities. Kept. A seat written immediately before the group seat + eye + god is the plain case of a doubled sign; Budge marks it (sic); the "alternatives" are not readings the papyrus supports: st on this papyrus is always seat + t + house (ani-022-072, the hymns, the Spell 125 introduction) and ꜣst always seat + t + egg (line 124 of this part, ani-017-b, the weighing); and st wsir would give "the place of union of the seat of Osiris", which says nothing. So the sense allows one reading, which is the condition the conventions set. The note now says why (see Changes). Q1 stays in the glyphs, `phon` with empty `tr`, as published unread signs (Z9).
- U12 "pure is Horus, divine(?) is Seth" — grammar confirmed: pḥ·n is the sḏm·n·f (morph pḥ + sḏm·n·f, the published analysis of ii·n·f) with rrt as nominal subject; twri ḥr and nṯrty stẖ are each predicate-first sentences of quality, as nfr X; twr is the published lemma (to be clean, pure; to cleanse) and nṯri a correct new lemma (the causative would be s-nṯr, as the note says). The unexplained endings i / ty are stated; the l "pure · Horus · divine(?) · Seth" mirrors the order. Left.
- U11 agentless passives "(by) Atum", "(by) the Double-Lion" — the supplied "by" is shown in parentheses in l, the note says in is not written and the reading is not sure, and offers the vocative "your house is built, Atum". An active sḏm·f is excluded by the order (pr·k before tm would make the house the builder). Left; i not hedged further, as the doubt is in the note in plain words.
- U11 l "is-built / is-founded" against i "has been built / has been founded" — l marks the passive and i gives its perfective sense in English; not a contradiction. Left.
- U13 iṯ·n·f X1 as `comp` with `tr` ṯ — the reading has no t; the conventions give a complement the consonant it repeats; the note says ṯ and t had fallen together. ani-017-b's iṯt has X1 `phon t` because its reading has the t. Left.
- U3 / U4 / U5 / U6 / U7 / U8 / U9 / U13 / U14 — re-read word by word against the packet and Budge's transliteration (Budge's maat for irt, seś for swꜣ and his single "rer" for the oblong of ṯs-pẖr are handled in the notes); names and `say` (Khepri, Ra, Isis, Nephthys, Anubis, Osiris, Shu, Neni-nesu, Horus, Seth, Atum, Ruti, Ani, Tanenet) agree with the published parts; red/black statements in the notes agree with the rubric flags. No change.
- gloss tꜣnnt, ḥs, ꜥfdt, mꜥẖtw, qnqn, smꜣt, rrt, ntf — general to the lemma, labels right, "(?)" where the notes doubt, Budge's spelling given for the names and rare words. ntf's "ntf N 'he is N'" is the general construction, not a quote. Left.
